content:
December is almost here, and so is one of our favorite coding traditions! We’re excited to take part in Advent of Code once again and invite you to join us for another season of festive puzzles, clever Kotlin solutions, and friendly competition.

Advent of Code is a great opportunity to learn something new and have fun along the way. Here’s what’s planned for this year:

  • Four days of livestreams (December 1–4) with Kotlin Developer Advocate Sebastian Aigner and special guests from the Kotlin team and community, exploring different approaches to solving the puzzles.
  • A welcoming community in Kotlinlang Slack, where you can exchange ideas, share solutions, and help each other out.
  • Kotlin leaderboards and exclusive prizes for the top performer, a randomly selected participant, and an outstanding community contributor

Four days of festive coding, live

From December 1 to 4, join Sebastian and a different guest each day as they work through the Advent of Code puzzles in Kotlin.

Discover new ways to use Kotlin’s features, explore alternative solutions, pick up a few tricks, and join the conversation on Slack!

Join the #advent-of-code channel in Kotlinlang Slack.

Join the Kotlin community and leaderboards

If you enjoy a bit of friendly competition, join one of our Kotlin leaderboards on adventofcode.com. Go to the Leaderboard section of your Advent of Code profile and enter one of the following codes:

  • Leaderboard 1: 2553782-ea9e5df5
  • Leaderboard 2: 2553918-5c580ce9
  • Leaderboard 3: 3240094-10740dfa

Please join only one leaderboard to leave room for other participants.

How to win prizes

This year, we’ll once again be rewarding participants for their problem-solving skills, a little bit of luck, and their contributions to the Kotlin community.

For a chance to win exclusive Kotlin prizes:

  1. Solve at least three Advent of Code 2026 puzzles in Kotlin without using AI.
  2. Publish your solutions on GitHub and add the aoc-2026-in-kotlin topic to your repository.
  3. Make sure we can contact you through your GitHub profile by including an email address, X handle, or Bluesky handle.

To add the topic, open your GitHub repository, go to the About section, click the gear icon, and enter aoc-2026-in-kotlin in the Topics field.

You don’t have to be the fastest to win a prize. We’ll also recognize randomly selected participants and community members who make Advent of Code in Kotlin a welcoming and supportive experience.

Enjoy the challenge – Solve it yourself

Anyone can generate a quick solution now, but there’s still something especially rewarding about figuring things out yourself.

As the Advent of Code creator puts it:

If you send a friend to the gym on your behalf, would you expect to get stronger?

Get ready to code

Here are a few resources to help you get started:

  • Advent of Code Kotlin template.
  • Instructions on how to use the template.
  • Advent of Code in Kotlin solutions from previous years.

Happy coding, and see you on December 1!
